A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEMANTICIST study. All 20 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction, generation and representation results, ablations, and an appendix human-perception study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ImageNet experiments, ablations and human-perception results, including Table 1 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The encoder, diffusion decoder, nested CFG and autoregressive procedure are retained. Section 4.3 replaces the shared-null-token description with plural null tokens, matching the position-specific tokens already documented in v1 Appendix C.1; this does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet reconstruction, class-conditional generation, linear-probing and CLIP evaluations, together with the same human-perception comparison. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same tokenizer and generator comparators, including TiTok, ImageFolder, LlamaGen, CRT and MAR. The human-study distractor construction is also unchanged. Newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated resolution, training budgets, token configurations, metrics and human-test exposure times remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 newly documents the existing linear-probing setup without reporting a revision to an earlier setting.

E4.justification: Decoder-scale, CFG, REPA and token-dimensionality ablations, spectrum analyses, semantic evaluations and qualitative examples are retained. The REPA and dimensionality plots exchange figure numbers, without changing the analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates, curves and averaged human-preference scores. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1's entries are unchanged, including SEMANTICIST's DiT-L/DiT-XL rFID values of 0.78/0.72 and gFID of 2.57 for both. Matched plots and qualitative examples retain the same results throughout the appendices.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same score decomposition, orthogonality argument, variance hierarchy and assumptions. The main mathematical definitions and training equations are also unchanged; differences are typesetting and placement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of PCA-like token structure, semantic-spectrum decoupling, approximately 10% better reconstruction FID, competitive 32-token generation and up to 63.5% linear-probing accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of token hierarchy, diffusion-based decoupling, REPA and scaling remain substantively unchanged. The limitations and broader-impact discussion moves intact from the main text to the supplement.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.3 specifies that linear probing uses sklearn, frozen encoder weights, token representations and no data augmentation. The revised null-token wording also improves consistency with existing implementation details. These are documentation refinements.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to One-d-piece and Dieleman's Generative modelling in latent space, acknowledges similar dropout techniques in concurrent tokenizers, and explicitly contrasts its RGB encoder with FlexTok's VAE-token input. FlexTok was already discussed in v1 Appendix B.1.

P1.justification: v2 makes grammar and terminology edits, updates affiliation and acknowledgments, adds the short linear-probing subsection, and moves the author-contribution and limitations statements into the supplement. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 adds an explicit noise input and a dashed image-to-decoder connection. Appendix Figures 11 and 12 exchange numbering/order, several plots and qualitative figures are relocated or resized, and spacing and captions are adjusted.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility through Appendix C.3 and internal consistency by reconciling the null-token description with the existing implementation. The clearer architecture diagram and expanded concurrent-work acknowledgment also help readers. These are useful, limited gains; the empirical evidence and theoretical argument remain unchanged.
